mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a >0.25% decrease in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a >0.5% increase in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a 3-month increase in RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a quarter signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a >2% decrease in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a >300,000 increase in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% each within a quarter signals robust economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a >5% increase in both HOUST and RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a >0.5% increase in CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% in a quarter signals an economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a >1% decrease in GDPC1.
